issue: Can a defendant be convicted of attempted bank robbery under the first paragraph of 18 U.S.C. § 2113(a) without using actual force, violence, or intimidation in the attempt?

sides.position: The phrase "by force and violence, or by intimidation" modifies both "takes" and "attempts to take," so attempted bank robbery requires actual force, violence, or intimidation.
cases: United States v. Thornton, 539 F.3d 741 (7th Cir. 2008)
United States v. Bellew, 369 F.3d 450 (5th Cir. 2004)
United States v. Brown, 412 F.2d 381 (8th Cir. 1969)
United States v. Armstrong, No. 21-11252 (11th Cir. Dec. 11, 2024)

sides.position: Attempted bank robbery under § 2113(a) does not require actual force, violence, or intimidation; the attempt need only be a substantial step toward a taking.
cases: United States v. Stallworth, 543 F.2d 1038 (2d Cir. 1976)

this_court: requires actual force, violence, or intimidation for attempted bank robbery (the majority's position, which the Jordan opinion says is the minority view)
quote: We recognize that our sister circuits are divided on this question.
cite: United States v. John Armstrong, Jr., No. 21-11252 (11th Cir. 2024)
